title: Bit manipulation
body:
## The mental model
Bit operations expose compact set and parity representations, but the language’s integer model matters. Java int and JavaScript bitwise operations are 32-bit; Python integers are arbitrary precision and negative values behave like an unbounded sign extension.

## Worked example
For n=12 (1100₂), n-1=11 (1011₂), so n&(n-1)=8 (1000₂): the lowest set bit was cleared. Repeating counts set bits rather than iterating every possible position.

## Common mistakes
Right shift may preserve a sign bit. JavaScript >>> converts to unsigned 32-bit form, but shifting by 32 wraps the count modulo 32.

## A rule worth keeping
State signedness and width, especially at the highest bit and for negative inputs.

## Put it to work
Before opening the related exercise, predict one tiny case on paper, name a boundary where your reasoning could fail, and write the invariant or guarantee you intend to preserve. After testing, compare the observed result with your prediction. Explain a mismatch rather than merely changing the answer.

### Self-check
- [ ] I can explain the worked example without rereading it.
- [ ] I can construct a boundary case and explain its expected behavior.
- [ ] I can name a cost, limitation, or tradeoff of this technique.
- [ ] I can distinguish a practice result from a production guarantee.
